solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Explosions shattered brick safe

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so the letters of these two words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Explosives have been used to blow open a brick-built safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' looks like a description of the safe, but it signals an anagram of BRICK SAFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Engines that backfire make sudden bangs, so the noun is a plural word for loud blasts.

clue.text: Mark could show spirit if extended

definitions.meaning: a mark such as a trade name, or a mark burnt into cattle hide
add one letter and the word becomes a spirit distilled from wine

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint rather than a plain definition: lengthen the word by a Y and you get BRANDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A trademark or burnt identifying sign is this word; with a Y on the end it is the spirit distilled from wine.

clue.text: Homeric character devours appetizer served over bread

indicators.note: something that devours takes food inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a character, or letter, of Homer's Greek alphabet: chi

indicators.note: in this down clue, served over means the snack is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a tapa is a small Spanish appetizer

explanation.surface: A hero from Homer's epics wolfs down a starter before the bread arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homeric character' suggests Achilles or Odysseus, but it means a letter of Homer's Greek alphabet; 'served over' reads the snack upwards, giving APAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened flatbread from South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Language, almost lecherous, that's heard in the pit?

parts.note: French is a language

indicators.note: almost means the word falls just short, losing its last letter

parts.note: horny is slang for lecherous or randy

explanation.surface: A suggestive remark in a foreign tongue is overheard in some dark pit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pit' is the orchestra pit below a theatre stage, where this brass instrument plays; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: This brass instrument plays in the orchestra pit, so it is something whose sound comes from there.

clue.text: Skate over artificial material

parts.note: the skate is a flat fish of the ray family
on can mean over, as in a lid on a jar

explanation.surface: Someone skates across a surface made of synthetic stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skate' reads as a verb, but it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic fibre made from cellulose, a man-made fabric.

clue.text: First class actress in play takes flight

indicators.note: takes means the rearranged letters take another piece inside them
letters in play are loose and moving about, so the word actress is rearranged

parts.note: A1 means first-class; the digit 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A top-rated actress in a stage play takes off on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel; here it is a flight of stairs. 'in play' makes STRCASE, which 'takes' the first-class mark inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a run of steps between floors in a building.

clue.text: Season finally passes by

parts.note: a season is a period or time of year

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word passes

explanation.surface: Toward the end of the season, time goes by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word at the end, but it is the definition, as in 'three by four'.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, 'three by four' means three multiplied by four.

clue.text: Horse-racing paper covering sport from down under

indicators.note: in a down clue, down under means read from the bottom upwards, so the whole thing is read backwards
the paper covers the sport by wrapping round it

parts.note: FT, the Financial Times, is a newspaper
RU is short for rugby union

explanation.surface: A racing newspaper reports on an Australian sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' suggests Australia; in this down clue it means FRUT is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The turf is a name for the sport of horse-racing, from the grass of racecourses.

clue.text: Time after time held up by Lufthansa's premier jet?

indicators.note: after places the first word's piece after the second's
in a down clue, something held up by another piece sits above it, so the airline's letter goes at the bottom

parts.note: min is short for minute, a time
an era is a long period of time

indicators.note: premier means first, so take the first letter of Lufthansa's

explanation.surface: An airliner keeps being delayed by the German carrier's flagship jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jet' suggests an aircraft, but jet is a black stone; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet is a black fossil stone, a classic example of a mined substance.

clue.text: Queen's call for attention received by heroes at sea in unspecified location

indicators.note: one piece is received inside the other
at sea means confused, so the letters of heroes are mixed up

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, and a mew is the cry a cat gives for attention

explanation.surface: The Queen calls for the attention of heroes lost at sea somewhere unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' reads as the monarch but means a female cat. 'at sea' makes SOHERE, which has 'received' the cat's cry inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere means at a place not named or known.

clue.text: School hidden by mysterious facade moved to the west

indicators.note: west is to the left, so facade is moved in front of mysterious
the answer is hidden in these words, but only once they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A school sits behind a strange, mysterious front.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the order of the words so 'facade' comes first: in FACADE MYSTERIOUS the answer is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school or college, often a specialist one.

clue.text: Something like radar created by mate before lunch, apparently

indicators.note: the word is put together by fitting the friend inside the morning

parts.note: am is morning, the time before lunch
a crony is a close mate or pal

explanation.surface: A word made up by a friend before lunch, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radar' is an acronym of 'radio detection and ranging'; 'apparently' admits that AM is loosely 'before lunch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is a word formed from the initials of a phrase, the classic example of the type.

clue.text: Extreme position taken by crank in mortuary?

definitions.meaning: the point of a crank's turn where it lines up with the connecting rod and cannot drive it
read as a place for dead people, a centre for the dead

explanation.walkthrough: 'crank' reads as an eccentric person, but it is the engine part; the question mark flags the punning second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineers name the crank's stalled straight-line point so; a mortuary is jokingly a facility for corpses.

clue.text: Plan reviewed tower block walls

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed, looked at again from the other end, so the letters run backwards
the words tower block wall in, or enclose, the letters

explanation.surface: A scheme is being reconsidered for a tall residential building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walls' hides WERB in 'tower block', and 'reviewed' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To brew trouble or a plot is to devise or prepare it.

clue.text: Discussion document produced by political activist on the Guardian?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a Green is an environmental political activist
The Guardian is a newspaper

explanation.surface: A political campaigner writes a policy piece in a left-leaning newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK, a government's preliminary policy proposals for discussion are called a GREEN PAPER.
explanation.definitionFit: The British government issues these consultative proposals before firm legislation.

clue.text: Kinky stuff leading to sex with hotel guest on dirty weekend?

parts.note: S and M, sadomasochism, is kinky stuff
it is a coy word for sex appeal or sex
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Something kinky leading to sex with someone staying at a hotel on an illicit weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: Couples on an illicit weekend traditionally signed hotel registers as 'Mr and Mrs Smith'.
explanation.definitionFit: The common surname is the stock false name used by adulterous couples checking into hotels.

clue.text: Doctors generally order this sort of fuel

definitions.text: Doctors generally order this sort of fuel

parts.words: Doctors generally order this sort of fuel
parts.note: read as advice a GP gives smokers, two words telling them to cut down, which is also a kind of fuel

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer is the order doctors give heavy smokers; whole, it is a fuel that burns cleanly.
explanation.definitionFit: This fuel, such as anthracite, burns without giving off soot, as required in UK clean-air zones.

clue.text: Steps taken in court — trouble about cases

parts.note: a quad, or quadrangle, is a courtyard

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: re means about or concerning
ill means trouble or harm

explanation.surface: Measures taken in a law court lead to trouble about the cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' and 'court' suggest legal action, but the steps are those of a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrille is an old square dance for four couples, made up of set steps.

clue.text: Action, originally repeatedly denied, to bolster share price

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that bolsters another sits below it, holding it up

parts.note: a quota is a share or allotted portion

indicators.note: the first letter is removed, and then the new first letter is removed again

explanation.surface: Action is repeatedly blocked at first, but then shores up the company's share price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'share price' looks like one phrase, but 'share' is QUOTA and 'price' the definition. ACTION loses its first letter twice, leaving TION.
explanation.definitionFit: A quotation is a price quoted, as for a job or a stock.

clue.text: Deliberately back up floppy Spooner possesses

indicators.note: possesses means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other
something floppy is loose and shapeless, so the letters of Spooner are rearranged
back means the word up is read backwards

explanation.surface: Back up a floppy disk on purpose, as the Reverend Spooner might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner' promises a Spoonerism, but it is plain anagram fodder: 'floppy' makes ONRPOSE, which 'possesses' PU, from 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with intent or by design is the same as doing it deliberately.

clue.text: What, in short, could make personal assistant sore?

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: writing out PA in full could make personal assistant, so this phrase means in full

explanation.surface: What, briefly, might make a personal assistant hurt?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'what could make personal assistant' as PA IN FULL; 'in short' then trims the last L. The parse is loose, and the blogger was unsure of it too.
explanation.definitionFit: Something painful hurts, just as a sore spot does.

clue.text: Predator heading away from hound

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, is taken away from the dog

parts.note: a beagle is a hunting hound

explanation.surface: A predator runs off from a hunting dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading away' reads as fleeing, but it means removing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This large bird of prey hunts small mammals and fish.

clue.text: Refreshed magically, having been exposed and frozen

indicators.note: refreshed means made new again, so the letters are rearranged
exposed means stripped of covering, so magically loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something magically revived after being left out in the cold, frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been exposed' strips MAGICALLY of its first and last letters, leaving AGICALL, which 'Refreshed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Glacial means icy cold, like a glacier.

clue.text: Go to live apart from society

indicators.note: apart from means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to exist is to live

explanation.surface: Go off to live separately from the rest of society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to live' reads as one phrase, but 'Go' alone is the definition, a verb meaning leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to leave a room or stage, so it is a verb for leaving.

clue.text: Essentially crazy couple walk out, disregarding officer's initial warning

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
the essence of a word is its centre, so take the middle letter of crazy
disregarding means leaving out, so a letter is removed from couple
initial means the first letter of officer's

explanation.surface: A crazy couple storm out, ignoring the officer's first warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A (centre of 'crazy'), COUPLE without O (first of 'officer's') and WALK, and 'out' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A wake-up call is a jolting alert that something must change.

clue.text: Old Bill could become this precise

parts.note: ex means former, or old
a parliamentary bill becomes an act once passed into law

explanation.surface: The police might become exacting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police; here 'Old' and 'Bill' work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise or accurate.

clue.text: Cunning of a king playing to the audience?

indicators.note: the audience hears the word, so it is said aloud

parts.note: Lear is the king of Shakespeare's tragedy, so of a king suggests an adjective formed from his name

explanation.surface: The cunning of a king who plays up to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king; 'Lear-y' would mean 'of Lear', and spoken it matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Leery means wary or suspicious; the older sense is knowing or sly.

clue.text: Cancel party at country club

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is jokingly a club of countries
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Cancel the party at the local country club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country club' suggests golf, but it is the United Nations, a club whose members are countries.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo is to reverse or cancel an action.

clue.text: Steffi, having lost way to begin with, carries final to secure title

indicators.note: carries means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other
having lost means letters are taken away from the name Steffi

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: Steffi Graf, having lost her way early, holds on to win the final and the title.
explanation.walkthrough: Steffi Graf is a tennis champion, which steers toward winning a title. 'to begin with' says the way comes off the front, leaving EFFI to carry the final.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi is a Turkish title of respect, like 'sir'.

clue.text: Give notice to schoolmaster about to cut a degree course

indicators.note: to cut means to break into a piece, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: PPE, philosophy, politics and economics, is an Oxford degree course

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sir is how pupils address a schoolmaster

explanation.surface: Inform a headmaster that he is about to drop a degree course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SIR into RIS, which cuts into A PPE. PPE is a well-known Oxford degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone is to inform them of something.

clue.text: Shots fired, at first sporadically, over very large area in revolution

indicators.note: at first means the first letter of sporadically
in revolution means turned around, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
L is short for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Gunfire breaks out sporadically over a wide area during a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' reads OVLA backwards to give ALVO, after S from 'sporadically'.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns.

clue.text: Spontaneously go cycling around America with friend

indicators.note: around means one piece goes round the other
cycling moves the last letter round to the front

parts.note: a go is a turn
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Naturally, they go cycling around the States with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves TURN's last letter to the front, giving NTUR, which goes 'around' A after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting naturally means acting without effort or contrivance.
